$comment: CUE TEXT FOR VARIANTS THE PROGRAMME DOES NOT PRESCRIBE, so the swap control can offer them.
RECOVERED 2026-08-31 from content/gym/program.json at git eadb279, the programme live before the
whole-week rebuild. That file carried 82 alt entries with cue text typed into program.json, and
the rebuild dropped every one because it built each slot from scratch. Four probe-gym checks
caught it; no static gate did, because an absent optional field looks exactly like a field
nobody wanted. He uses the swap control: gym_set.swapped_from records 13 distinct swaps, the
most recent on 2026-08-27, four days before this file existed.
THIS FILE HOLDS NO CUE FOR ANY PRESCRIBED EXERCISE, on purpose. A prescribed slot carries its own
cue in program.json and that is the one the card renders; a second copy here would be a second
copy of a fact, which is what inProgramme was and why it was deleted. scripts/gym-alts.mjs
asserts the two sets stay disjoint and refuses to run if they overlap.
THE RIGHT LONG-TERM HOME IS movements.json, on the variant, because a cue describes how to do a
movement and is the same for every slot that prescribes it. That is a larger change than the
session that wrote this could verify, so it is written down rather than done.

lateral-bound AND db-lateral-lunge WERE REMOVED FROM HERE 2026-09-01, when both were restored to the programme. Their cues now live on their slots in program.json, which is the single source the card renders. gym-alts.mjs refused to run while both copies existed, which is that guard doing its job on its first real occasion.

SIX CUES ADDED 2026-09-01, so the swap control can offer exercises his gym has and the programme does not prescribe. Five are RECOVERED from program.json at d707ae7~1, the commit before the 2026-08-27 cut, with their placement clauses trimmed: that is text he was already reading, which beats anything an agent composes. One is DRAFTED, for smith-hip-thrust, the exercise he named by name on 2026-09-01, from the methods section of HealthOS/knowledge/sources/plotkin-2023-hip-thrust.html. Its two position tests are that paper verbatim: "Repetitions were considered properly executed when the participant's tibia was perpendicular to the floor and the femur was parallel to the floor", and the bottom is "brief contact with the ground ... at the bottom of each repetition". Tempo is theirs too, "a concentric action of approximately 1 s and an eccentric action of approximately 2 s", as is the stance, "feet spaced 1-1.5-times shoulder width apart". It says DRAFT in the text he reads, because nobody has watched him do it, and AGENTS.md reserves reporting that a cue failed at the machine to him alone.

TWO CITATIONS WERE STRIPPED 2026-09-01, and both were surfaced by the cross-group swap rule rather than introduced by it: these cues existed already and were simply never offered, so nothing had ever checked them. half-kneeling-sa-press cited THE MOTION BLUEPRINT, which he ordered dropped on 2026-08-27, so the citation went and the technique description stands on its own. db-incline-press quoted Rodriguez-Ridao et al. 2020 (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17:7339) at length with EMG figures by bench angle, and THAT PAPER IS NOT SAVED ON THIS DISK: a source not in HealthOS/knowledge/sources/ is not a source, and nobody could check those quotes. The claim is now stated as something he can test on himself, with a doneness cue he can actually perform. THE PAPER IS ON THIS DISK NOW, fetched 2026-09-03 to HealthOS/knowledge/sources/rodriguez-ridao-2020-bench-inclination-emg.txt, so the sentence above saying it is not saved is no longer true and this is the correction. The full text is paywalled; the free abstract carries the angle findings and they are: 30 trained adults at 60% of 1RM across 0, 15, 30, 45 and 60 degrees, with peak EMG for the UPPER pectoralis at 30 degrees, for the middle and lower portions at 0 degrees, for the anterior deltoid at 60 degrees, and the triceps similar at every angle. So the angle numbers are available and checkable if they are ever wanted back. Nothing has been put back into any cue: this is the source, not a decision.

cues.pogo-hops: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.
cues.box-step-up-explosive: One foot on the box. Drive up fast enough that the other foot leaves the ground at the top, then lower slowly. No jumping, so no landing. Use this if anything hurts. 3x5 each leg.
cues.smith-squat: On rails. Feet slightly forward of the bar. Same depth, no balance demand.
cues.heavy-goblet-squat: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.
cues.leg-press: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.
cues.db-rdl: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.
cues.back-extension: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.
cues.kb-swing: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.
cues.db-step-up: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.
cues.reverse-lunge: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.
cues.single-leg-leg-press: One foot in the middle of the platform. Light enough that the working leg does all of it. 8/leg.
cues.suitcase-carry: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.
cues.kb-suitcase-hold: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.
cues.lateral-step-up: Stand side-on to the box. Step UP sideways onto it with the near foot, drive through that heel, lower slowly. 3x8/leg.
cues.banded-lateral-walk: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.
cues.single-leg-calf-raise: One leg at a time holding one dumbbell, full range. Harder, and closer to what running actually asks of the ankle. 3x12/leg.
cues.bench-press: Barbell version. Same shoulder blades, same pause on the chest. Easier to load heavy, harder on the shoulders.
cues.machine-chest-press: A press on a machine, moderate rather than heavy: the barbell bench is where the press gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.
cues.db-incline-press: Bench one or two notches up from flat, dumbbells. About 30 degrees, which is one or two notches, not half way up. More work for the top of the chest and the front of the shoulder, less for the middle and lower chest. Your note #31 asked what the difference is: neither is better, they are different halves of the same muscle, and the steeper you go the more the shoulder takes over. Success looks like: you feel it across your collarbone rather than under your nipple line. If your shoulders are doing all of it, lower the bench a notch. If you are doing this instead of flat, SWAP TO IT on the card so your log says what you actually pressed.
cues.hollow-hold: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.
cues.side-plank: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.
cues.half-kneeling-sa-press: One knee down, the other foot forward, one dumbbell in the hand on the SAME side as the down knee. Press it straight overhead without letting your ribs flare or your body lean away. It is two exercises at once: a press, and your trunk refusing to bend sideways under a load held on one side. Lighter than the two-dumbbell version by a lot, and that is the point.
cues.bb-ohp: Barbell from the rack at collarbone height. Push your head slightly back so the bar clears your face, then forward under it at the top.
cues.machine-shoulder-press: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, not above your ears. Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging, and come back down slowly until the handles are level with your shoulders again. Stop the set when your lower back starts arching off the pad.
cues.db-seated-ohp: Bench upright, back supported. Takes the lower back out of it entirely.
cues.assisted-pullup: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.
cues.pullup: The bar over the rack. Dead hang, chin over the bar, lower under control. As many clean reps as you have.
cues.trx-row: Straps at the pull-up bar. Body straight, pull your chest to your hands. Walk the feet forward to make it harder. 4x10.
cues.cable-overhead-tricep-extension: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the high pulley. Take the handle overhead, then bend only your elbows to lower it behind your head until you feel a stretch down the back of your arms, about level with the base of your skull. Your upper arms stay pointing at the ceiling and DO NOT drift forward: that is the whole exercise. Straighten the arms to come back up. Success looks like: your elbows stay the same distance apart the whole time and your ribs do not flare forward. If your back arches, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
cues.db-skullcrusher: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, bend at the elbow to lower them beside your ears and press back up. Use this if overhead bothers your shoulder.
cues.tricep-pushdown-alt: The cable version, only if the stack you are already standing at is free between sets.
cues.seated-cable-row: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.
cues.chest-supported-row: Chest on an incline bench, dumbbells hanging. The bench removes the lower back entirely, so nothing can cheat. Good on a day the RDLs left your back tired.
cues.db-lateral-raise-seated: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.
cues.kb-lateral-raise: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.
cues.tricep-pushdown: Cable high, rope or straight bar. Pin your elbows to your sides and keep them there: only the forearms move. Push down until the arms are completely straight, hold half a second, then let it come up slowly until you feel the stretch. If your elbows drift forward or you lean over the bar, drop the weight.
cues.ez-skullcrusher: Lying on a bench with the EZ bar. Keep the upper arms still and pointing at the ceiling, bend only at the elbow to lower the bar toward your forehead, then straighten. Light.
cues.db-curl-supinated: Same movement with the palms turned UP the whole way instead of facing in. Same muscle, slightly different angle.
cues.kb-hammer-curl: A kettlebell in each hand by the handle, same elbow-pinned curl. The weight hangs behind your hand, which makes the top half harder.
cues.cable-pallof: Set the cable at chest height. Stand SIDEWAYS to the machine and step away from it until the cable is already TIGHT with the handle held against your breastbone, arms bent: if there is slack before you start, you are too close. Feet shoulder width. The cable is now trying to twist you toward it. Press your hands straight out in front of your chest until the arms are locked, hold for two seconds, and come back to your breastbone. The whole exercise is refusing to rotate. TWO CHECKS YOU CAN DO ALONE, and they replaced one that needed somebody standing behind you: (1) keep your eyes on a fixed point on the wall straight ahead, and if your hands drift out of the middle of your chest towards the machine as you press, you are rotating. (2) Your feet must not move. If either foot slides or you have to re-plant it during a set, go lighter. Do all reps one side, then turn around.
cues.band-pallof: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.
cues.half-kneeling-pallof: Same press, kneeling on the knee CLOSEST to the machine with the other foot forward. Kneeling takes the legs out of it, so the only thing that can stop the twist is your trunk. Harder at the same weight.
cues.cable-reverse-fly: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the adjustable cable column, standing tall, a handle in each hand and a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
cues.chest-supported-reverse-fly: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.
cues.pec-deck-rear-delt: The fly machine turned around. Arms out and back, squeeze the shoulder blades, no jerking.
cues.lateral-line-hop: The easier version. Both feet together, hop side to side over a line on the floor, small and fast, staying on the balls of your feet. 3x15.
cues.smith-rdl: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.
cues.leg-curl: Lying or seated depending on which machine is free. Set the pad so it sits just ABOVE your heels, on the Achilles, not on your calf. Lie or sit with your knees lined up with the machine pivot, the bolt the arm turns on. Curl your heels toward your bum as far as the machine allows, pause for one second at the tightest point, then lower slowly, taking about twice as long down as up. Success looks like: your hips stay flat on the pad and do not lift as you curl. If they lift, go lighter. This is the only exercise in the week that bends the knee against resistance: every other hamstring movement here is a hinge, where the hamstring works at the hip instead.
cues.walking-lunge: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.
cues.b-stance-rdl: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.
cues.kb-single-leg-rdl: Same movement holding a kettlebell. The handle sits closer to your leg, which some people find easier to control. 8/leg.
cues.copenhagen-plank: The groin and inner-thigh half of the sideways work, and the piece nothing in the old programme trained at all. START WITH THE EASY VERSION: lie on your side with your bottom forearm on the floor, and put your TOP KNEE (not the foot) on the bench. Lift your hips off the floor so your body is a straight line, squeezing the bench with the top leg. Hold for the seconds shown. Your bottom leg hangs free. When 3 sets of 20 seconds feels controlled, move the top FOOT to the bench instead of the knee, which is much harder. Expect this to be humbling. Stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin. Count the seconds in your head, one thousand one, one thousand two: you are on one forearm and cannot reach the phone. The count is the number you type.
cues.adductor-squeeze: The gentlest version. On your back, knees bent, a ball or rolled towel between the knees. Squeeze it hard for the seconds shown and breathe. 3x20s.
cues.side-plank-leg-lift: Side plank on the forearm, then lift the TOP leg toward the ceiling and hold. Trains the outside of the hip instead of the inside. 3x20s per side.
cues.stability-ball-ham-curl: The version their programme actually names, if the machine is taken and a ball is free. On your back, heels on the ball, hips lifted, roll the ball in toward you by bending the knees, then roll it back out slowly without letting the hips drop.
cues.glute-back-extension-alt: On the 45 degree pad, hugging a plate. Not the same movement, it works the hamstring at the hip like everything else here, but it is the closest thing if the leg curl is taken.
cues.pec-deck: Elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring the arms together in front of you and squeeze for one second. Stretch, not a press.
cues.lat-pulldown-alt: If the assisted machine is taken. Same job, elbows down to the ribs, all the way straight at the top.
cues.db-ohp-seated: Bench upright, dumbbells at shoulder height, press up and slightly together. Ribs down, no arch.
cues.straight-arm-pulldown: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.
cues.band-straight-arm-pulldown: Band anchored high on a rack post. Identical arc with straight arms. Use it when the cables are all busy.
cues.db-pullover: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.
cues.incline-db-curl: A dumbbell in each hand on the incline bench. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.
cues.bicep-curl: Standing, dumbbells, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.
cues.cable-curl: Low cable with a straight or EZ attachment. The cable keeps tension on the muscle at every point, including the top where dumbbells go light. 3x12.
cues.hammer-curl: Thumbs up the whole way, like holding two hammers. Hits the forearm and the outside of the arm too.
cues.kb-farmer-carry: Kettlebells instead, and THE RACK STOPS AT 50 LB EACH: that is the whole set, 20 up to 50, two of each. His note #18, 2026-08-25: 'Therea no kettlebell after 50 for farmers'. He is right, and it is why the prescribed version is dumbbells, which go to 90 and which he has already carried at 75 per hand. Use this one when the dumbbells are taken, not when you want it heavier. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder at the same weight.
cues.db-hold: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.
cues.single-leg-glute-bridge: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.
cues.frog-pump: On your back, soles of the feet together, knees fallen wide, heels close to you. Push the hips up and squeeze the glutes hard at the top for one second, then lower. The knees stay wide the whole time. This position forces the glutes to lead instead of the hamstrings. 3x20.
cues.plank-shoulder-taps: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.
cues.banded-hip-abduction: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds at the widest point, then let them come back slowly. Success looks like: you feel it on the outside of the hip, above and behind the hip bone. 3x15.
cues.clamshell: On your side, short band above the knees, knees bent 90. Open the top knee like a clam without letting your hips roll backwards. Success looks like: your top hip stays stacked over the bottom one. If you have to roll back to open further, you have gone as far as it goes. 3x15 each side.
cues.smith-hip-thrust: DRAFT, not yet used at the machine: tell the note box what is wrong with it. Set the Smith bar low on the rails. Sit on the floor with your upper back on a bench behind you, the bar across your hip crease with a pad under it, feet flat and about one and a half shoulder widths apart. Drive your hips up. Success looks like TWO things you can see: your shins are vertical, straight up and down like a table leg, and your thighs are level with the floor. Not higher. If your ribs flare and your lower back arches to get there, you have gone past the top. One second up, two seconds down. Come back until your hips just brush the floor between reps. 3x8.
cues.db-overhead-press: STANDING, not seated: that is the difference between this and the seated version in the alternatives, and it is why this needs no bench. Done second in the session from 2026-08-22, and the reason is in "Why this is here". Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward. Squeeze your bum and tighten your stomach BEFORE you press, so your ribs do not flare and your lower back does not arch. Press straight up until the arms are locked out with the dumbbells over the middle of your head, not in front of your face. Lower under control to the shoulders. Success looks like: your ribs stay down and you can hold the lockout still for a second. If your back arches to start the rep, go lighter.
cues.db-lateral-lunge: This is the sideways movement you asked for, and it is loaded on purpose: unweighted band walks were shown to do little. Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Step wide to the LEFT and sit back into that left hip, keeping the right leg straight with the foot flat. Both feet stay pointing forward the whole time. Push off the left foot to come back. You should feel a stretch on the inside of the straight leg and work in the bent leg's hip. Start with a light dumbbell and a small step, then widen the step before you add weight.
cues.lumbar-extension: NEW, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT EXERCISE FROM THE ONE YOU HAVE BEEN DOING ON THIS MACHINE. Same frame, opposite instruction. On the back extension you have logged since June you hold your back FLAT and your hip does the moving. Here your hip stays put and your BACK does the moving. That is the only way anything in your gym trains the muscles either side of your spine as the thing that moves you rather than the thing that holds on. START WITH NO WEIGHT AT ALL, arms crossed on your chest, and do not add any until this is easy: the weights on your other back extension do not carry over, and starting there is how people hurt themselves on this. HOW TO SET UP. Same as the other one. Hip pad top edge just below your hip bones, ankles under the rollers, feet flat. HOW TO DO IT. Start standing tall in the frame. Let your upper back curl down first, then your middle back, then your lower back, one bit at a time, the way you would roll down a wall. Three seconds down, and only as far as is comfortable, which the first few times will be about half the range. Then reverse it: lower back first, then middle, then upper, until you are standing tall again. STOP AT TALL. Do not arch backwards past it. Success looks like: the work is low down, in a band across your waist, and the next day feels like a working ache rather than anything sharp. Ten to fifteen reps. STOP AND TELL ME if you get anything sharp, anything that shoots down a leg, or anything still there the next morning. This one is a draft written for you and you are the only person who can say whether it works, so use the note box under it after the first session either way.
cues.db-overhead-tricep-extension: Standing, one dumbbell held in both hands behind your head, elbows pointing up and staying pointed up. Straighten your arms to lift the weight overhead without letting your elbows drift out sideways. Lower until you feel a stretch under the arm. Success looks like: your elbows stay in the same place the whole set and only your forearms move. If your elbows flare, go lighter.
cues.cable-crunch: Kneel facing the pulldown machine with the rope at the top. Hold the rope beside your ears and let your elbows stay there the whole set: the arms do not pull. Curl your ribs down towards your hips so your back rounds, then come back up slowly. Success looks like: the movement happens between your ribs and your hips and nowhere else. If your hips are folding and your back stays flat, you are doing a hip hinge on your knees, not a crunch. Start light enough that you can do it slowly.
cues.db-calf-raise: Standing on the floor in the rest between lunge sets, a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides. Feet about hip width. Push all the way up onto your toes, as high as you can go, and hold for one second at the top. Then lower slowly, about three seconds down, until your heels touch the floor and you feel a stretch through the back of the calf. Success looks like: you can hold the top position still for a second without wobbling, and the slow way down is what you feel most. If you cannot hold the top, the dumbbells are too heavy. This is the flat-floor version, so the stretch at the bottom is smaller than on the machine; that is the trade for it costing you no walk.

TWO CITATIONS TO A DROPPED SOURCE WERE REMOVED FROM THIS FILE ON 2026-09-03: cues.cable-pallof and cues.leg-curl both ended by crediting The Motion Blueprint. Only the citation sentence went; not one word of instruction changed.

He ordered that guide dropped: "the conclusion was that that program wasn't really that good so drop it, i dont care." HealthOS/knowledge/training-programme-evidence.md records it and ends "Nothing may keep citing it."

AND THIS FILE WAS INVISIBLE TO THE GATE THAT ENFORCES THAT, which is the finding worth keeping. knowledge/check-sources.mjs walks a hand-named PROGRAM_TEXT_FILES list of three files, program.json, equipment.json and movements.json. alt-cues.json was never in it, so these two citations sat in rendered cue text for twelve days while the gate reported on the identical defect in program.json and went green on these. The list is now derived from the directory instead of typed, so a new content file under content/gym is covered the day it is created.

BOTH CUES ARE NOW UNSOURCED AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. The evidence file already says the leg curl and the "eight core patterns" claim behind the Pallof press "now have no source at all and must either be re-sourced or removed." No replacement was invented. The instruction that survives in each is machine setup, tempo and a success test, which never rested on that guide.
